properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S IDEA, 2026-08-09, close to verbatim: "adding some type of usage-log tool that captures what reflow2 skills and tools were used in a session would be a nice utility. maybe a tool is not the right option, but something that AUTOMATICALLY logs (maybe store it in project graph?) usage and issues (DOESN'T DIAGNOSE, JUST LOGS)."

⭐ HIS OWN DOUBT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART AND IT IS CORRECT. **A TOOL IS THE WRONG SHAPE, and self-defeatingly so: a tool must be CALLED, and the population most worth measuring is precisely the one least likely to call it.** An agent that forgets `revise-design` forgets `log_usage`. The measurement would be biased toward the sessions that need no measuring. Every MCP call already passes through the server, so the server can record without the agent's cooperation — which is the only way the number means anything.

"DOESN'T DIAGNOSE, JUST LOGS" IS ALREADY THIS PROJECT'S DOCTRINE, not a new constraint: `dec:report-dont-judge` holds that the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. Same shape, one domain over.

--- WHERE IT LIVES: THE QUESTION HE FLAGGED ---

(1) BESIDE THE STORE, NOT IN THE GRAPH — the recommendation. The graph is the DESIGN; usage is telemetry about a SESSION and belongs to the process, not to the design. Putting it in the graph means every export carries it (already 4.1 MB), every diff churns with it, and `compare_designs` reports telemetry as design divergence. `rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global` draws the same line from the other side: the test is whether a second design open in the same process would need a different value, and session usage would not. PRECEDENT EXISTS AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — reflow2 already keeps session-scoped state beside the store rather than inside it (the shared-mode rendezvous and log; `shared.rs` pins "log sits beside the store too" and "rendezvous sits beside the store NOT INSIDE IT").

(2) IN THE GRAPH — what it would buy: usage becomes queryable with the same tools as everything else, and survives in the export. COUNTER: it makes the design record grow with facts that are not design, and the export is the thing consumers merge.

⭐ THE RESOLUTION THAT USES BOTH, and it is an existing pattern rather than a compromise: LOG RAW TO THE SIDECAR, PROMOTE FINDINGS DELIBERATELY. `dec:manifest-derived-is-not-manifest-accepted` already holds that a bulk derivation is not a bulk accept and writes nothing until asked. Raw usage is derivation; a finding worth keeping ("this rule was violated four times") is something a human accepts INTO the design.

--- WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS ---

**NOBODY HAS EVER MEASURED SKILL USAGE.** `dec:bl-155` measured TOOL calls — 6,095 across 46 retained transcripts — and found 40 of 132 tools never called. There is no equivalent for `get_skill`, which is server-side and trivially countable. So `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` proposes to improve a rate NOBODY HAS EVER OBSERVED, and without this instrument there is no way to tell whether any hint changed anything.

⚠️ AND BL-155'S CAVEAT TRAVELS WITH IT, because it is the trap: absence is WEAK evidence. `set_project_mode` appeared as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls despite having been used. A tool can be discussed far more than used; a skill can be FOLLOWED FROM MEMORY without being fetched, which this session did for revise-design. **So a usage log measures FETCHES, not COMPLIANCE, and reporting it as compliance would be exactly the false confidence the loop exists to prevent.**

--- OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS ---
- Does it log ISSUES as well as usage (his words: "usage and issues")? A refusal is already visible to the server; recording refusals would surface the enum-rejection class of defect without anyone filing a report.
- Is it opt-in? `dec:idea-measure-the-surface` already asks how far usage telemetry may go, and this is that question made concrete.
- Retention. `dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size` says what bounds a store is WHAT gets stored, not how big it is.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Recorded so the shape is chosen deliberately rather than by whoever builds it first.
properties.name: OPEN — how should reflow2 log which of its own skills and tools a session used, and where does that log live?
properties.rationale: Anthony's idea, with his own doubt about the tool shape carried into the record rather than smoothed away, because that doubt is the part that decides the design. Kept OPEN rather than accepted: the storage question turns on how far telemetry may go, which is already an unanswered decision (dec:idea-measure-the-surface), and answering it here by implication would settle it without him.
